title: Trunk-Based Development & Release Workflows
summary: Quick revision notes on trunk-based development, short-lived branches, GitFlow's CI cost, release branches, merge queues, semantic versioning with tagging, and monorepo path-filtered pipelines.

chapters.title: Trunk-Based Development: The Mental Model
points: Trunk-based development: everyone integrates into one main branch (trunk) at least daily; trunk is always releasable
Integration frequency is the core metric: branches live hours to ~2 days, never weeks
Incomplete work ships dark behind feature flags, so merging never means releasing
Trunk-based vs GitFlow: one long-lived branch vs main + develop + release + hotfix branches
Trunk stays green only with fast automated tests on every commit and a rule that a broken trunk is fixed or reverted first

chapters.title: Short-Lived Feature Branches in Practice
points: Cycle: git switch -c feat/x from fresh main, commit small, open PR, merge, delete branch same day
Keep PRs small (about 200-400 lines changed); small diffs review fast and conflict rarely
Rebase onto main before merging: git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main keeps history linear
Squash merge gives one commit per change on trunk and makes reverts a single git revert
Branch by abstraction or feature flag splits big refactors into steps that each merge safely
Mistake: a long-running branch that drifts and ends in a painful merge; sync main daily or merge in slices

chapters.title: GitFlow and Why It Slows CI
points: GitFlow branches: main (releases), develop (integration), feature/*, release/*, hotfix/*
Features merge into develop only when finished, so integration is delayed and merge conflicts pile up
CI runs against many long-lived branches, multiplying pipeline runs and duplicate builds
Hotfixes must be merged back into both main and develop; forgetting one reintroduces the bug
Release is gated by a stabilization branch, so lead time from commit to production is days or weeks
Fits versioned, multi-release products (installed software); poor fit for continuous deployment of web services

chapters.title: Release Branches, Merge Queues and Tagging
points: Release branch (release/1.4) is cut from trunk only when you must support old versions; fixes land on trunk first, then cherry-pick: git cherry-pick -x <sha>
Merge queue tests each PR on top of the PRs ahead of it, then merges, so main never breaks from a semantic merge conflict
Enable GitHub merge queue via branch protection; CI must also trigger on the merge_group event
Semantic versioning MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH: breaking change bumps MAJOR, new compatible feature MINOR, bug fix PATCH; 1.2.3 to 2.0.0 resets lower numbers
Tag releases as annotated: git tag -a v1.4.0 -m "Release 1.4.0" then git push origin v1.4.0 (tags are not pushed by default)
Mistake: moving or reusing a published tag; ship a new patch version instead

chapters.title: Monorepo Pipelines with Path Filters
points: Path filters run a pipeline only when relevant files change, e.g. GitHub Actions on.push.paths: ['services/api/**','libs/shared/**']
Include shared dependency paths (libs/, lockfile, the workflow file itself) or dependent services skip tests they need
Use paths-ignore for docs-only changes (docs/**, *.md) to skip CI entirely
Required status checks plus path filters deadlock: a skipped workflow leaves the check pending; fix with an always-run job that detects changes (dorny/paths-filter) and gates downstream jobs
Per-service tags like api-v1.2.0 let each service version and release independently; trigger deploy on on.push.tags: ['api-v*']
Mistake: shallow clone with fetch-depth: 1 breaks change detection against the base branch; fetch the diff range

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Branching, Release and CI
points: Trunk daily: git switch -c feat/x; git fetch && git rebase origin/main; squash merge; delete branch
Rule of thumb: branch lifetime under 2 days, PR under ~400 lines, trunk always green
Pick model: trunk-based for continuous deploy; GitFlow only for versioned, multi-release products
Release: git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m msg; git push origin vX.Y.Z; fix on trunk, git cherry-pick -x to release/X.Y
SemVer: MAJOR breaking, MINOR feature, PATCH fix; never reuse a published tag
Monorepo: paths filter including shared libs, always-run change-detect job, merge_group trigger for merge queue
